dress_code.men: Dhoti/Kurta (Devotees are encouraged to wear modest and traditional Indian attire while visiting the temple and participating in rituals)
dress_code.women: Saree/Churidar (Devotees are encouraged to wear modest and traditional Indian attire while visiting the temple and participating in rituals)

dos: Wear modest and traditional Indian attire (Dhoti/Kurta for men, Saree/Churidar for women) while visiting the temple and participating in rituals.
Bathe only at designated safe ghats equipped with security chains/railings.
Follow instructions broadcasted over the public address system.
Keep children close during the annual 3-day Jatara (Maha Shivaratri).
Watch out for pickpockets during major festival crowds.
Contact the Temple Control Room/Administrative Office near the main entrance for Lost and Found assistance.
Contact on-duty supervisors or administrative staff directly at the Administrative Office near the entrance gates for emergency contacting of temple authorities.
donts: Strictly avoid entering the river or attempting to swim when warning signs are placed during monsoons (July to September) or when Singur Dam gates are opened upstream.
Do not wear footwear (shoes/slippers) beyond designated holding counters or inside the temple sanctum.
Do not consume alcohol, meat, or tobacco products anywhere near the sacred temple premises.
Do not engage in photography or videography inside the restricted inner cave shrine (garbha griha).
